text:
Sam: quick experiment thought — rather than full lease swap for short cross-region bursts, what about 'delegated observer proxies' that issue short-lived write-delegate tokens and keep the local proxy active for reads? idea is reduce p99 for regional writes while avoiding risky full primary handoff for transient traffic. looking for tradeoffs + rollout plan.

Maria: high-level: are we mainly targeting tail latency on geo reads/writes or reducing the frequency of swap handoffs?

Sam: mainly tail write latency for EU/APAC from local edge -> avoid 100–200ms extra when we do a full lease swap for a tenant that just spiked. reads still local. writes are forwarded but can be accepted locally if token present.

Chen: sketch: proxy (delegatee) requests a signed token from the primary region: {region: eu-west-1, epoch: 1234, expires: t+20s, nonce, sig}. token authorizes a small set of write ops (monotonic id range) and is revocable. primary still owns final authoritative state; delegatee applies write locally as provisional and ships to primary async. on conflict, primary returns conflict + resolution.

Ravi: main concerns: deletes and idempotency. how do we guarantee forward progress on conflicting ops? if delegatee keeps local tentatives, we can end up with divergent tombstones. need a conflict-resolution contract (last-write-id? vector clock?).

Sam: agree. thinking of adding per-tenant monotonic write-id (server-assigned at token mint) + server-side merge rules. for deletions, require a confirm roundtrip for destructive ops unless token has explicit destructive flag.

Chen: proto sketch (proxy header):
```
X-Region-Delegate: region=eu-west-1;epoch=1234;expires=1715009999;sig=BASE64SIG
```
client->edge proxy accepts write when header valid. edge writes to local sstable (provisional) and streams to primary via reliable queue. primary validates sig/nonce, assigns final seq, reconciles.

Maria: good. for rollout: 1) unit tests for signature/expiry/nonce, 2) canary with 1% tenants in eu region, 3) fault-injection where primary acks are delayed/dropped to see divergence behavior.

Ravi: metrics to instrument: p99 write latency (tenant), %writes accepted by delegation, conflict rate (per 1k delegated writes), reconciliation lag (time between local provisional write and primary commit), and percent of tokens revoked. also an alert for >0.5% unresolved conflicts per minute.

Sam: fallback plan: if conflict rate or revocations exceed thresholds, proxies stop delegating for that tenant and trigger a normal lease swap + telemetry export. also automatic revocation endpoint on control plane: /delegation/revoke?tenant=..

Chen: test plan additions: chaos test where delegated writes are split-brained for 10s; verify that reconciliation converges and client-visible order is preserved or deterministic. add e2e with embeddings/kv workloads and cold-cache scenarios.

Ravi: security note: token audience must be scoped and short-lived; integrate KMS signing and record minting events in audit logs. also rate-limit token requests to avoid local hot tenants minting tokens rapidly.

infra-bot: canary created: infra/canaries/delegate-observer-1715009999 — monitors: canary.p99_write_latency, canary.delegation_conflict_rate, canary.reconciliation_lag

Sam: action items: @Chen to draft proto + header format (this week). @Maria to write rollout playbook and canary thresholds. @Ravi to add conflict detection + reconciliation tests. I'll wire up quick proxy support and a hook for automatic revocation.

Maria: sounds good. one more: add a legal/data-residency check — delegated acceptance should only be allowed if tenant residency policy allows provisional buffering in primary region. can't sidestep residency rules.

Sam: noted — will add residency gate at mint time.

Chen: +1 on residency gate. also we should log delegation-token→primary-commit mapping for auditability.

Ravi: ok. if we keep tokens tiny (20s) and conservative flags (no deletes by default), seems low-risk. canary metrics will tell.

Sam: thanks all — I'll post the RFC-draft link once Chen has the proto. :thumbsup:
